[Discussion] Any good examples of games which have imbalance in gameplay but use it so well that you want to experiment with suboptimal items/stats/characters etc.?

Do you mean imbalance like "rock beats scissors beats paper beats rock"? I think Rainbow Six: Siege actually does a good job of this. Every operator you play as has one or two hard counters, which in turn are countered by something else. There's no on at the top of the totem pole, and odds are good that there's someone on your team that can defend you against whatever your Achilles heel is. I find myself jumping from operator to operator to try and figure out where they sit in the network of checks and balances.

If you haven't watched it before, Extra Credits has a fantastic episode about this:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e31OSVZF77w

If you want to read more, just google 'mtg jedi curve'. Its a game design philosophy by which unbalance actually creates more dynamic gameplay.
